transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

My thoughts won’t slow down, and it’s gotten to the point where I can’t focus enough to do my work safely. I'm a pipefitter apprentice, and I'm just really overwhelmed because my brain is constantly running and I feel like I can't keep up with it.
Have you noticed your mood feeling unusually high, irritable, or overly energetic at any point recently, in addition to your racing thoughts?

Yes, I definitely swing into these high periods where I feel on top of the world, like snapping selfies on the scaffold at 2 a.m., but then I'll suddenly blow up at my foreman or boyfriend over nothing. During those times, I'm so energetic that I can't stop moving—I'll volunteer for double shifts, stay up reorganizing my whole apartment, and sign up for random certifications at midnight.
How long do these high or irritable periods usually last—do they last for several days or longer, and have you ever had one that lasted a week or more?

Yes, they definitely last for several days or even weeks at a time. Over the last five months of this rollercoaster, I've had stretches lasting a week or more where I felt constantly energized, stayed up late working on layouts, and felt on top of the world. But during those same weeks, my mood could also swing instantly and I'd get incredibly irritable.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["F31", "F30"], but based on this conversation, F30 (Manic Episode) is no longer a strong candidate because the patient reports recurrent episodes of mood elevation and irritability lasting for several days to weeks, along with impaired functioning over a prolonged period of at least five months, which meets criteria for a bipolar disorder with a pattern of recurrent manic and likely depressive or mixed episodes. F31 (Bipolar Affective Disorder) is now the only appropriate candidate as it accounts for the episodic nature of both elevated/irritable mood and the chronic fluctuating course described. The presence of multiple distinct episodes with significant functional impairment supports this diagnosis over a single manic episode (F30).

inference_history.note: Previously the candidates were [F30, F31, F32, F41], but based on the patient's description of distinct mood elevation with increased energy, decreased need for sleep, impulsivity (e.g., snapping selfies at 2 a.m., reorganizing apartment, signing up for certifications), and irritability alternating with high periods, bipolar spectrum disorder is strongly indicated. This makes F32 (depressive episode) and F41 (other anxiety disorders) less likely as standalone diagnoses, since there is clear evidence of manic symptoms. F30 (mania without psychotic symptoms) and F31 (bipolar affective disorder) remain as candidates, with F31 being more likely if there have been recurrent episodes. The presentation suggests a recurrent pattern, so F31 is favored, but F30 is retained pending further clarification on episode recurrence.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits clear episodes of mania with increased energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, impulsivity, and irritability lasting over a week, meeting criteria for bipolar I disorder. The recurrent nature and significant functional impairment support this diagnosis.
